elements.quote: Objective: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the study aim using the term 'systematically' and that it is assessing CPGs, identifying the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: Objective: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a clear main objective/review question describing what was to be identified and assessed.

elements.quote: We included any guideline that provided recommendations on the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the main inclusion criterion (guidelines with recommendations for critically ill COVID-19 patients) but does not state any exclusion criteria in the abstract.

elements.quote: We searched Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, CNKI, CBM, WanFang, and grey literature from November 2019 - November 2020.
elements.reason: The abstract lists the information sources searched and gives the date range, indicating when searches were conducted (up to November 2020).

elements.quote: We assessed the quality with the AGREE II instrument
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the instrument used to assess the quality (risk of bias/quality) of included guidelines (AGREE II).

elements.quote: We descriptively summarized CPGs characteristics. We assessed the quality with the AGREE II instrument and we summarized relevant therapeutic interventions.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the methods of presentation and synthesis as descriptive summary of guideline characteristics and interventions.

elements.quote: We retrieved 3,907 records and 71 CPGs were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included records and included CPGs (71) and provides summary characteristics (AGREE II domain scores).

elements.quote: Means (Standard Deviations) of the scores for the 6 domains of the AGREE II instrument were 65%(SD19.56%), 39%(SD19.64%), 27%(SD19.48%), 70%(SD15.74%), 26%(SD18.49%), 42%(SD34.91) for the scope and purpose, stakeholder involvement, rigor of development, clarity of presentation, applicability, editorial independence domains, respectively. Most of the CPGs showed a low overall quality (less than 40%).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (AGREE II domain scores and overall quality) and reports the number of included CPGs related to these outcomes.
No meta-analysis was conducted; the abstract indicates descriptive summary methods rather than any pooled quantitative synthesis.
The abstract does not report any group comparisons requiring direction-of-effect statements; synthesis was descriptive.

The abstract does not briefly summarize limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision) even though it reports low overall quality, no explicit limitations statement is provided in the abstract.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Future CPGs for COVID-19 need to rely, for their development, on standard evidence-based methods and tools.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and implications for future guideline development.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding; funding is reported elsewhere in the paper but not in the abstract.
The abstract does not provide the register name or registration number; registration (PROSPERO ID) is reported in the Methods section, not the abstract.

elements.quote: A possible explanation might be the extreme conditions under which these CPGs were developed including global uncertainty about the natural history of the COVID-19 infection, the lack of direct evidence, and external pressures to produce rapid advice, lack of technical capacity to develop high-quality CPGs, among others. Moreover, the continuously evolving evidence landscape of COVID-19 would require an ongoing process of monitoring and updating as some recommendations are likely to change [96].
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the current state (evolving evidence, lack of direct evidence) and important uncertainties affecting guideline development.

elements.quote: Given the extraordinary burden that the pandemic has created on the emergency and critical care units worldwide, there is an urgent need for evidence-based guidance to facilitate optimal clinical and policy decisionmaking.
elements.reason: The authors explain the importance and need for the review, citing the pandemic burden and the urgent requirement for evidence-based guidance for critical care.

elements.quote: Four previous reviews have assessed the quality of COVID-19 CPGs [16-18]. Two of them focused on the CPGs produced in the early phase of the pandemic. Zhao et al. evaluated CPGs for 5 different viruses, including SARS-CoV2, that have caused public health emergencies of international concern over 20 years, with search date ending February 2, 2020. Dagens et al. study focused on the early stage of the pandemic, with search date up to March 14, 2020 [1]. ... However, an assessment of all the CPGs focused on the management of critically ill COVID -19 patients was lacking. We, therefore, aimed to systematically identify the CPGs for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19, and critically assess their quality for both clinical and methodological purposes.
elements.reason: The manuscript cites prior reviews and explicitly states a gap (lack of comprehensive assessment for critically ill patients), justifying the need for the current review.

The review is of clinical practice guidelines for critical care rather than a review of intervention effects; no proposed mechanism of action for specific interventions is described in the provided evidence.

No logic model or hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes are presented; the manuscript focuses on appraisal of guidelines rather than evaluation of complex interventions.

elements.quote: Objective: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: The review objective is explicitly stated (to identify and critically assess CPGs for critically ill COVID-19 patients using AGREE II), but it is not presented using a recognized question-formulation framework (e.g., PICO or similar).

elements.quote: Objective: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: The review focuses on identifying and assessing clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) rather than evaluating intervention effects; therefore planned comparisons in PICO format for intervention effects are not applicable.

elements.quote: Selection criteria For inclusion, CPGs had to provide specific recommendations for clinical management, diagnosis and/or treatment of critically ill patients with COVID-19. When more than one version was available, we included only the most updated version or edition of the eligible RGs.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the target population (critically ill patients with COVID-19) and the type of documents (CPGs providing specific recommendations) and a rule for multiple versions, but does not fully specify other study-eligibility characteristics requested by the checklist (e.g., eligible study designs beyond CPGs, settings, follow-up requirements, or full question-framework components).

elements.quote: We conducted a comprehensive search the most important databases, and we did not apply any language restrictions. ... the assessments were conducted only on CPGs that were either published in peer review journals or posted in official websites as CPG full documents, without considering unpublished or supplementary material, therefore, it is possible that some information was missing to inform the quality of the CPGs in this iteration but it is planned to be covered in the following series of this living review.
elements.reason: The review states language policy (no language restrictions) and limits on publication/report status (only peer-reviewed or official website CPG full documents), but does not report any criteria about dissemination year or other report-characteristic restrictions, so reporting of report-characteristic eligibility is incomplete.

elements.quote: Selection criteria For inclusion, CPGs had to provide specific recommendations for clinical management, diagnosis and/or treatment of critically ill patients with COVID-19.
elements.reason: This review assesses clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) rather than primary studies measuring outcomes; the retrieved evidence contains no information on excluding reports because outcomes were not measured versus not reported, so the outcome-based distinction does not apply to this guideline-focused review.

elements.quote: The table summarizes the scope of the recommendations. Each row shows the most common interventions of interest in critical patients with COVID-19 (general supportive care and therapeutic interventions). The second column displays the number of guidelines that cover each recommendation, and the following columns describes the guidelines that provide recommendations for each intervention of interest categorized as Low, Moderate or High quality according to AGREE score obtained in domain 3.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies how guidelines were grouped in the syntheses (rows by interventions; columns by number of guidelines and by quality categories: Low/Moderate/High linked to AGREE D3), which links synthesized groups to comparisons of interest.

elements.quote: We had to exclude, for now, CPGs that were written in languages that were not covered by our research team (i.e., Japanese).
elements.reason: The authors state a notable restriction (exclusion of CPGs in languages not covered by the team) and provide a rationale (language coverage limitations), satisfying the requirement to justify notable eligibility restrictions.

elements.quote: An electronic database search was conducted from November 1, 2019 to October 1, 2020 by a health sciences librarian (LH) in Medline (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCO), Embase, China national knowledge infrastructure (CNKI), China Biomedical Literature database (CBM), and WanFang Data. ... Grey literature search (e.g., CPG databases and repositories and official websites of relevant critical care or intensive care professional societies as a part of snowballing) was conducted across more than 20 different resources and was extended until November 30, 2020.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports overall search date ranges for the databases (Nov 1, 2019 to Oct 1, 2020) and a date for when grey literature searching was extended (until Nov 30, 2020), but does not report the specific last-search date for each individual information source.

elements.quote: An electronic database search was conducted ... in Medline (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCO), Embase, China national knowledge infrastructure (CNKI), China Biomedical Literature database (CBM), and WanFang Data. The CPGs search filter from the CADTH database ( https:// www.cadth.ca/ ) was translated to CINAHL; and Embase to text words and relevant index terms.
elements.reason: The names of the bibliographic databases and some search interfaces/platforms are reported (e.g., Medline (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCO)), but coverage dates for each database are not provided and some platforms (e.g., Embase) are not fully specified; therefore reporting is incomplete.

No evidence provided that any study register, regulatory database, or online repository was searched with named sources and date restrictions; the text lists databases but does not report searching study registers or their date restrictions.

elements.quote: The CPGs search filter from the CADTH database ( https:// www.cadth.ca/ ) was translated to CINAHL; ... Grey literature search (e.g., CPG databases and repositories and official websites of relevant critical care or intensive care professional societies as a part of snowballing) was conducted across more than 20 different resources ...
elements.reason: The CADTH website and its URL are explicitly reported, but other websites and online sources are referred to generically ("official websites" and "more than 20 different resources") without names or URLs.
There is no explicit statement naming organisations or manufacturers that were contacted to identify studies.
The manuscript does not describe types of individuals contacted to identify studies (no evidence of contacting individuals or their roles).
Although "snowballing" and grey literature searches are mentioned, the authors do not specify the types of reference lists examined.
No details are provided about backward or forward citation searching (no seed reports, citation index/platform, or search dates reported).
The authors do not report consulting specific journals or conference proceedings with source names, dates covered, or search methods.

elements.quote: An electronic database search was conducted from November 1, 2019 to October 1, 2020 by a health sciences librarian (LH) in Medline (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCO), Embase, China national knowledge infrastructure (CNKI), China Biomedical Literature database (CBM), and WanFang Data, The CPGs search filter from the CADTH database ( https:// www.cadth.ca/ ) was translated to CINAHL; and Embase to text words and relevant index terms. A search strategy was developed using the keywords that cover all the possible terms and synonyms for COVID-19 and the CPGs. Grey literature search (e.g., CPG databases and repositories and official websites of relevant critical care or intensive care professional societies as a part of snowballing) was conducted across more than 20 different resources and was extended until November 30, 2020. Search strategies are described in the (Supplementary material). No language restrictions were applied at the outset.
elements.reason: Databases searched, date ranges, and that full search strategies are in the supplementary material are reported, but the complete search strings as actually run for each source are not presented in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: An electronic database search was conducted from November 1, 2019 to October 1, 2020 ... Grey literature search ... was extended until November 30, 2020. ... No language restrictions were applied at the outset.
elements.reason: Date limits and statement of no language restrictions are reported, but justification of these limits by reference to the eligibility criteria is not provided in the evidence.

elements.quote: The CPGs search filter from the CADTH database ( https:// www.cadth.ca/ ) was translated to CINAHL; and Embase to text words and relevant index terms.
elements.reason: A published search filter (CADTH CPGs search filter) is cited and the adaptations (translation to CINAHL and conversion for Embase) are described.
No mention of natural-language processing or text-analysis tools used to identify or refine search terms in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: The CPGs search filter from the CADTH database ( https:// www.cadth.ca/ ) was translated to CINAHL; and Embase to text words and relevant index terms.
elements.reason: The authors state that the CADTH filter was translated for other databases, indicating translation occurred, but they do not specify which tools or methods were used to translate search strings between sources.
No description of any validation of the search strategy, validation process, or validation studies is provided in the retrieved evidence.
There is no information about peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) or the process/tool used in the provided evidence.
No information is provided about the conceptual structure used for the search (e.g., non-PICO structure) or explorations used to develop it.

elements.quote: One reviewer independently screened the retrieved titles and abstracts. A second reviewer screened the undecided and included for quality control. After the first screening, 2 reviewers screened the full text independently, and a third reviewer was invited to resolve disagreements.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly reports the number of reviewers at the title/abstract stage (one primary, a second for undecided/included QC) and at full-text stage (two reviewers independently), satisfying the requirement.

elements.quote: One reviewer independently screened the retrieved titles and abstracts. A second reviewer screened the undecided and included for quality control. After the first screening, 2 reviewers screened the full text independently...
elements.reason: The text states that the initial screening was done independently by one reviewer and that full-text screening was done independently by two reviewers, thus reporting whether reviewers worked independently at each stage.

elements.quote: After the first screening, 2 reviewers screened the full text independently, and a third reviewer was invited to resolve disagreements.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the process for resolving screening disagreements (inviting a third reviewer) and elsewhere notes disagreements were resolved by consensus, meeting the requirement.
No evidence describing processes to obtain or confirm eligibility information from study investigators is provided in the retrieved text.
There is no information in the provided evidence about methods used to translate abstracts or full articles for eligibility assessment.

elements.quote: All screening and data extraction were conducted by importing the search results into an EndNote Library (version X9) and Google Sheets.
elements.reason: The authors report using EndNote and Google Sheets to manage screening and extraction, but do not describe any automation tools integrated into the selection process (e.g., automated screening, machine classifiers, or how these tools affected decisions), so reporting is partial.
No information is provided about externally derived classifiers, their versions/references, roles, or records removed prior to screening.
No evidence describes internally derived classifiers, their use, training, or validation.
There is no mention of machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping/prioritisation rules in the provided evidence.
No information on using crowdsourcing platforms or integrating them into study selection is present in the retrieved evidence.
The manuscript does not describe previously screened datasets used to eliminate records, nor how such datasets were derived.

elements.quote: Data extraction was performed independently and in duplicate by two reviewers.
elements.reason: Explicit statement that two reviewers performed data extraction in duplicate.

elements.quote: Data extraction was performed independently and in duplicate by two reviewers.
elements.reason: States that multiple data collectors worked independently (data extraction done independently and in duplicate).

elements.quote: After the first screening, 2 reviewers screened the full text independently, and a third reviewer was invited to resolve disagreements.
elements.reason: Describes a process to resolve disagreements by involving a third reviewer; additionally, text_1 notes "Disagreements were resolved by consensus."
No information provided about contacting study investigators to obtain or confirm data.

elements.quote: All screening and data extraction were conducted by importing the search results into an EndNote Library (version X9) and Google Sheets.
elements.reason: Specifies software used (EndNote, Google Sheets) for screening and data extraction but does not describe any automation tools' use, training, or validation.
No methods reported for translating articles for data collection; although no language restrictions were applied, translation methods are not described.
No software reported for extracting data from figures.

elements.quote: When more than one version was available, we included only the most updated version or edition of the eligible RGs.
elements.reason: Provides a decision rule for selecting among multiple versions of reports (choose most updated version).

No text explicitly lists or defines outcome domains for which data were sought. Extracted variables (text_5) describe guideline characteristics and therapeutic interventions but do not define outcome domains (e.g., mortality, length of stay, adverse events).
No information specifies the time frame of measurement for any outcome domain in the retrieved evidence.
The manuscript does not state whether all results compatible with each outcome domain (e.g., all measures, time points, analyses) were sought.
There is no description of a process used to select results when not all compatible results were sought; no selection methods for outcome results are reported in the provided evidence.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance (or rationales for such changes) are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains (or rationales) are described in the provided text.
The outcomes considered most important for interpreting conclusions and the rationale for their prioritisation are not reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We extracted the following variables from each eligible CPG: ID (acronym or first author), country, economic classification, healthcare system, scope of the CPG, language, methods of development, date of publication, developer organization (if applicable), type of organization, target critical disease (specialty), CPG implementation tools, consideration of patients' views and preferences, the use of specific method to assess quality of the evidence (e.g. GRADE), and all options of therapeutic interventions for critically ill people with COVID-19 whether general supportive care or specific COVID-19 therapy, results of the AGREE II quality assessments (See next section).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists the other variables extracted from each eligible guideline, matching the requirement to list and define variables sought.
No text in the provided evidence describes assumptions made about missing or unclear study information; no explicit statement of such assumptions was found.

elements.quote: This rapid and living systematic review was informed by three methodological guides for CPGs' systematic reviews, rapid reviews, and living reviews [ 8 , 19 , 20 ].
elements.reason: The authors cite methodological guides that informed the review (i.e., tools/guides used to determine methods and data collection), which fulfills the requirement to cite any tool used to determine which data items to collect.

elements.quote: Two reviewers conducted independent quality assessment of each eligible CPG with the AGREE II instrument, which consists of 23 items grouped in 6 domains, in addition to 2 final overall assessments.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly names the risk-of-bias / quality assessment tool used (AGREE II) and describes it as consisting of 23 items in 6 domains.

elements.quote: The six AGREE II domains are scope and purpose, stakeholder involvement, rigour of development, clarity of presentation, applicability, and editorial independence. The scope and purpose domain is concerned with the overall aim of the CPG, the specific health questions, and the target population; the stakeholder involvement domain focuses on the extent to which the CPG was developed by the appropriate stakeholders and represents the views of its intended users; the rigour of development domains relates to the process used to gather and synthesize the evidence, the methods to formulate the recommendations, and to update them; the clarity of presentation deals with the language, structure, and format of the CPG; the applicability domain pertains to the likely barriers and facilitators to implementation, strategies to improve uptake, and resource implications of applying the CPG; and the editorial independence domain is concerned with the formulation of recommendations not being unduly biased with competing interests.
elements.reason: The manuscript lists each AGREE II domain and describes what each domain assesses, fulfilling the requirement to specify domains/components assessed by the tool.

elements.quote: A final overall assessment includes the rating of the overall quality of the CPG (OA1) and whether the CPG would be recommended for use in practice (OA2).
elements.reason: The authors report that two overall assessments (OA1 overall quality and OA2 recommendation for use) were made. Additionally, elsewhere they specify a rule for overall quality (see below), indicating how at least one overall judgement was derived.
No information is provided in the retrieved evidence about any adaptations made to the AGREE II tool.
The manuscript reports using the established AGREE II instrument; there is no indication that a newly developed risk-of-bias tool was created for this review.

elements.quote: Two reviewers conducted independent quality assessment of each eligible CPG with the AGREE II instrument... The reviewers held discussions after completing the AGREE II assessments to avoid such variability or discrepancies. ... Discrepancies in the scoring were resolved by focus group discussions facilitated by a CPG methodologist (YSA).
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the number of reviewers (two) performing independent assessments and describes the procedure used to resolve disagreements (discussions and focus group facilitated by a methodologist).
The retrieved evidence does not describe any processes used to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias (AGREE II) information from study or guideline investigators.

elements.quote: We used the online platform MY AGREE PLUS ( https://www. agreetrust.org/ my-agree/ ) to run the appraisals [ 14 , 15 ].
elements.reason: An automation/online tool (MY AGREE PLUS) is named as being used to run the appraisals, but no further details are provided about how the tool was used, any training, performance, or validation of automation assistance.

The Methods and data extraction sections list variables extracted and describe processes, but there is no specification of effect measures (e.g., risk ratio, mean difference) for any outcome in the provided evidence.
No thresholds or ranges used to interpret effect size, nor any rationale for such thresholds, are reported in the provided Methods or Results text.
There is no description of methods used to re-express synthesized results using another effect measure in the retrieved evidence.
The provided sections do not justify the choice of any effect measure; no rationale or explanation for selecting effect measures is present in the evidence.

elements.quote: Selection criteria For inclusion, CPGs had to provide specific recommendations for clinical management, diagnosis and/or treatment of critically ill patients with COVID-19. When more than one version was available, we included only the most updated version or edition of the eligible RGs.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports clear inclusion criteria for eligible CPGs and a rule for selecting the most recent version, which addresses part of how studies were selected. However, it does not describe the specific processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis (for example, how CPG intervention characteristics were tabulated and compared against planned groups for each synthesis), nor how individual CPGs were assigned to particular syntheses—only summary tables of interventions are provided without an explicit procedural description.

elements.quote: We summarized the general characteristics of the CPGs with descriptive statistics. We present frequencies and proportions to summarize categorical variables used to describe the guidelines. We used mean and standard deviation (SD) to summarize the scores across all the guidelines per domain. ... Furthermore, we compared the clinical content of the eligible CPGs through a tabular summary of therapeutic interventions that were mentioned in the CPGs' recommendation.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes how extracted data were summarized (frequencies, proportions, mean and SD) and presented in tabular summaries, which documents methods for preparing data for presentation. However, it does not describe methods for handling missing summary statistics or any data conversions; therefore the reporting is incomplete.

elements.quote: The variables were extracted to an online Google sheet then later presented in tabular formats that were agreed upon after several online focus group discussion and brainstorming meetings with 2-4 reviewers as needed to reach final agreements.
elements.reason: Methods explicitly state that extracted variables were presented in tabular formats and that the tabular presentation was decided through meetings, describing the tabular structures used to display results.

elements.quote: Figure 1 displays the selection process through the PRISMA statement flow diagram [21].
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly reports using a PRISMA flow diagram to display the selection process, indicating at least one graphical method; however, no other graphical methods or details about visual displays of individual study results or syntheses are described in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: | Included Rapid Guidelines (RGs): Total number 71 (100%) - Low quality (D3: <40%)* | Included Rapid Guidelines (RGs): Total number 71 (100%) - Moderate quality (D3: 40-59%)* | Included Rapid Guidelines (RGs): Total number 71 (100%) - High quality (D3: ≥60%)* |
elements.reason: Tables show grouping/ordering of guidelines by quality categories (low, moderate, high), demonstrating an ordering/grouping within tables; however, the methods do not explicitly state the basis or rationale for choosing this ordering in the provided evidence.
No information is provided in the retrieved evidence about the use of non-standard graphs or the rationale for using them.

No statistical synthesis or meta-analysis was performed or described in the manuscript; software/packages for statistical synthesis are not applicable. The manuscript reports use of EndNote and Google Sheets for screening and data extraction, not statistical synthesis.

elements.quote: All screening and data extraction were conducted by importing the search results into an EndNote Library (version X9) and Google Sheets. ... The variables were extracted to an online Google sheet then later presented in tabular formats that were agreed upon after several online focus group discussion and brainstorming meetings with 2-4 reviewers as needed to reach final agreements.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes that extracted variables were presented in tabular formats and that Google Sheets/EndNote were used for extraction and presentation, which indicates an alternative (tabular) synthesis. However, no justification is provided for this approach nor an explicit explanation that meta-analysis was impossible, so the description is incomplete.

elements.quote: All reviews observed the overall poor quality of the majority of assessed CPGs [ 1 , 15 ] - [17] .
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly places the review's findings in the context of other published reviews, noting that those earlier reviews similarly observed overall poor quality of CPGs, thereby interpreting the results against other relevant evidence.

elements.quote: A possible explanation might be the extreme conditions under which these CPGs were developed including global uncertainty about the natural history of the COVID-19 infection, the lack of direct evidence, and external pressures to produce rapid advice, lack of technical capacity to develop high-quality CPGs, among others. Moreover, the continuously evolving evidence landscape of COVID-19 would require an ongoing process of monitoring and updating as some recommendations are likely to change [96]. ... However, this study is not free of limitations. We had to exclude, for now, CPGs that were written in languages that were not covered by our research team (i.e., Japanese). Moreover, the assessments were conducted only on CPGs that were either published in peer review journals or posted in official websites as CPG full documents, without considering unpublished or supplementary material, therefore, it is possible that some information was missing to inform the quality of the CPGs in this iteration but it is planned to be covered in the following series of this living review.
elements.reason: The discussion explicitly describes limitations of the included evidence (lack of direct evidence, evolving evidence requiring updates) and study limitations affecting the evidence included (language exclusions; only published or posted full documents considered), addressing limitations of the evidence included in the review.

elements.quote: However, this study is not free of limitations. We had to exclude, for now, CPGs that were written in languages that were not covered by our research team (i.e., Japanese). elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly lists limitations of the review processes (language exclusions and exclusion of unpublished/supplementary material).

elements.quote: Despite using only 2 appraisers meets the minimum standard for AGREE II, it potentially may reduce the reliability of results and increases the likelihood that betweenrater variability may directly affect the results.
elements.reason: The manuscript discusses the potential impact of a review-process limitation (use of only two appraisers) on result reliability and between-rater variability; additional impact (possible missing information affecting quality assessment) is noted in text_16.

elements.quote: Our results will be helpful for healthcare professionals, CPG developers, CPG users/implementers, and decisionmakers. Intensive care clinicians now have a summary of the available CPG and can choose among them the most trustworthy to follow. Developers and decision-makers can also choose from our list the CPGs that are of higher quality to eventually adapt or endorse a CPG to be used in their contexts.
elements.reason: The discussion explicitly states how the review results can be used by clinicians and developers to select, adapt, implement, or follow trustworthy guidelines — directly addressing implications for practice.

elements.quote: Developers and decision-makers can also choose from our list the CPGs that are of higher quality to eventually adapt or endorse a CPG to be used in their contexts. In summary, our work complements and aim to inform initiatives as RecMap and COVID-END to reduce duplication of efforts and facilitate dissemination of the guidelines' recommendations. Therefore, our team is committed to continue collaborating with these initiatives.
elements.reason: The discussion explicitly addresses decision-makers and policy-related uses (adapting/endorsing guidelines, informing initiatives, reducing duplication, facilitating dissemination), indicating implications for policy.

elements.quote: However, we acknowledge that further methodological research is needed to provide better guidance on RGs development.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly call for further methodological research to improve guidance on rapid guideline (RG) development, constituting a clear recommendation for future research.
